body.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) and every regular conditional law \(P(\,\cdot\mid z_0)\) of the complete causal-data array given the realized query, one has
\[
 P(\,\cdot\mid z_0)\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)
\]
for \(P\)-almost every query value \(z_0\) under its marginal query law.  No membership assertion is made for a version of the conditional law at a query-null value.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) and a regular conditional law \(P(\,\cdot\mid z_0)\).  We check the defining clauses of \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}.  The consistency, boundedness, exact-design observation, Holder, and interior clauses hold under \(P\); disintegration therefore makes their conditional versions hold outside a marginally null set of query values.  The conditional-expectation equalities in \texttt{ass:event-date-transport} and \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} are equalities of versions and hence also hold outside marginally null sets.

Assumption \texttt{ass:design-density} explicitly supplies, for every \(s,t\), a conditional density satisfying
\[
 c_X\le f_{st\mid z_0}(x)\le C_X
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in[0,1]^d
\tag{1}
\]
for almost every query.  Assumption \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing} likewise supplies
\[
 \beta_s(k\mid z_0)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
 \qquad k\ge1,
\tag{2}
\]
for almost every query.  The conditional-independence assertions in \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}, \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, and \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} are precisely factorization assertions for these regular conditional laws.  Thus they hold for almost every query.  Finally, \texttt{ass:donor-unbiasedness}, \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}, and \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment} give, for almost every query,
\[
 \mathbb E[Z_j\mid z_0]=z_0,
 \quad
 c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid z_0)\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd},
 \quad
 \mathbb E\!\left[\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\mid z_0\right]\le B^4.
\tag{3}
\]

There are finitely many cohorts and dates and only countably many lags \(k\).  Intersecting the conull query sets just described therefore leaves a conull set.  At every query in this intersection, (1)--(3) and the remaining checked clauses are exactly the member properties of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Hence \(P(\,\cdot\mid z_0)\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) there.  The argument deliberately says nothing about an arbitrarily selected conditional version on the complementary null set.
body.justification: This lemma separates a fixed-query statistical experiment from the almost-everywhere disintegration that links it to a causal panel law.
body.gap: It does not select or regularize conditional versions at query-null values.
body.consumer: All fixed-query risk, coverage, and model-audit statements use this bridge when transferred back to the panel class.
